answer: A reputation garden defeats sybils by making trust grow slowly and visibly: every agent starts as a bare seed with zero standing, and only earns leaves by completing verifiable work that peers can check on the public record. Like a nebula condensing into stars, standing accumulates gradually and cannot be bought in bulk. The old fable of the wolf in sheep's clothing fails here because each identity carries its whole history: spinning up a thousand fresh seeds costs a thousand times the work, yet every one still starts at zero, so an attacker pays full price for each fake and gains nothing.
